notes.title: Fixes to NG+, collision issues, crashes and more!
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

Thank you for answering the call and fulfilling your duty once more as the Striver, by ridding the land of Ire of the evil Gahars. We’re so happy to see all the positivity around the game, and have been working hard to fix commonly raised bugs and issues that our brave Strivers have encountered.

We’re happy to push our first patch for the full game, fixing a range of issues with New Game +, collision issues and other bugs. Read the full patch notes below:

[h3][b]Patch Notes - 21/05/2024[/b][/h3]
[b][list]
[*]Fixed some collision issues in Dunghaven. 
[*]Fixed some collision issues in Cinder Valley.
[*]Fixed some collision issues in Irelia.
[*]Adjusted some of the collisions in the final Dunghaven encounter. 
[*]Changed some enemy pathing in Rimehold. 
[*]Adjusted the aggression of some enemies in Rimehold. 
[*]Adjusted the Skull Demon placement in Irelia. 
[*]Reduced the HP of the Snail Queen enemy.
[*]Fixed the crash that would occur when viewing the 'Spectre' entry in the Morbid Menagerie.
[*]Cleaned up the cinematic meshes left behind after killing Acolytes that could be seen when revisiting levels. 
[*]Fixed the Strivers hair model when playing on 'Low' graphics settings.  
[*]Bol should now be more inclined to talk to the player in Dunghaven. 
[*]Minor tweaks to the Lava Giant and Carcass King enemies.
[*]Fixed NG+ Not saving correctly. 
[*]Fixed the Hag not showing up in NG+ if the player already has relics from the previous Cycle. 
[*]Fixed the Mastodon enemies collision issue when using the 1st Raging bull attack. 
[*]Fixed the Player sometimes being able to move whilst in the meditation animation.
[*]Fixed Steam Cloud Saves not downloading correctly.
[/list][/b]
These changes, specific to the Rimehold area, will also be reflected in the game’s Demo.

In addition to these fixes, we are also actively looking at community discussions and reviews to see how we can further balance the game. We’re aware that some enemies currently take too little damage at high posture, as well as riposte being very strong right now. We are looking into the best ways to address this. 

If you encounter any other bugs on your journey through Ire, please leave your bug report on our [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2171560/discussions/0/4331977981785818130/]dedicated reporting thread here.[/url]  We are monitoring these issues and will continue to fix as many issues as we can.

And please continue to leave your thoughts and feedback in discussions and reviews, we’d love to hear what you think about the game!

Magratheus bless you, Striver.

notes.title: The Music of Morbid: The Lords of Ire
notes.content:
Greetings, Striver!

In the last dev diary, we delved deep into the combat of the game. This month, we will hear about the music. Simo Talasranta, the court composer of Still Running, has written and produced the fully orchestrated original soundtrack of Morbid: The Lords of Ire. Hear from him, how the score of the game has more to it than meets the ear.

Watch the brand new feature video, "The Music of Morbid: The Lords of Ire", where Simo talks about his craft below:

[previewyoutube=_vzquxWI_Lk;full][/previewyoutube]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/fc10c018df5c11cd7f3ec42bac8db710827e360d.png[/img]

[h3][b]Morbid Motifs[/b][/h3]

The soundtrack of Morbid: The Lords of Ire has been composed using an interconnected network of leit motifs (musical themes). In addition to the Acolytes having their own themes, the game has three main motifs that present themselves in various rhythmic, harmonic, and instrumental combinations throughout your journey.

[h3][b]Musical Journey[/b][/h3]

A good example of the interconnected themes is the music in Hall of Redemption, which not only introduces all three main motifs, but also hides within its melody a phrase from each of the Acolytes’ themes. In other words, the music of the hub area subliminally sets up your entire journey, before you’ve barely embarked on it.

[h3][b]Instrumentation[/b][/h3]

For the most part, the soundtrack utilizes the instrumentation of a traditional symphonic orchestra accompanied by a choir. However, since the game is set across several realms with different cultures, some tracks take a steady step into the domain of fusion music, combining oriental, tribal, and even electric instruments into the mix.

[h3][b]The Acolytes[/b][/h3]

In Morbid games, the epic boss tracks have always been—and are still—the most prominent part of the score. They draw a stark contrast between the haunting desolation of the world, and the sudden piercing terror of the ungodly encounters therein.

Additionally, each Acolyte’s theme is carefully foreshadowed throughout the preceding level, so that once you reach the ruler of the realm, the thematic power of the boss music hits you that much harder.

[h3][b]The Culmination[/b][/h3]

Throughout the game, the three main motifs are prevalent, hidden in almost all the tracks. But only at the very end do they reach their full potential. In the final battle of the game, the three  main motifs collide, playing perfectly on top of eachother, concluding your journey in a fierce storm of the three melodies.


Morbid: The Lords of Ire Original Soundtrack will be released on Spotify and other music platforms together with the game’s release on May 17th 2024.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/fc10c018df5c11cd7f3ec42bac8db710827e360d.png[/img]

notes.title: Developer Diary #6 - Combat
notes.content:
Greetings, Striver!

Last month, we introduced some of the weapons and the four melee combat styles you can experience. This month, we will show you the main types of player movements you get to use in the game and how the combat has grown through the game’s development in Morbid: The Lords of Ire. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/fc10c018df5c11cd7f3ec42bac8db710827e360d.png[/img]

[h3]General Combat[/h3]
In Morbid: The Lords of Ire, combat is fluid like a dance - by keeping active, you can get the most out of combat and kill more enemies with ease. By timing your blocks and attacks, you are able to reserve more stamina and fare better in your battle against evil. 

[h3]Basic Attacks[/h3]
Swing your weapon to perform a range of combo attacks. Combos are different depending on your weapon class and wielding style. 

[h3]Rage Breaker[/h3]
When an enemy becomes Enraged it cannot be staggered. When you encounter a raged enemy, perform a Rage Breaker attack to break through before they regain their posture.

[h3]Riposte[/h3]
When an enemy hit is about to land on you, parry the strike and perform a brutal counterattack. It is important to keep in mind that some powerful attacks cannot be parried.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/534005715f8bcb2c1dd59f8b6511bca696a71a4c.gif[/img]
[h3]Perfect Block[/h3]
It is important to note that, while blocking, your stamina regenerates at a slower rate. However, perfectly timed blocks restore Stamina, impact enemy Posture, and also rebound most projectiles.

[h3]Critical Blow [/h3]
Once enemy posture is gone, you can perform a Critical Blow on the staggered foe.
This deals enormous amounts of damage and is often lethal. This move also fully restores the Striver’s stamina bar. In some situations, you may choose to use the Spectre Blaser instead to deliver the Critical Blow.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/1cf3100f9dbcfe33acf1f6da8369baf54bb046d6.gif[/img]

[h3]Sneaking and Backstab[/h3]
Sneaking allows the player to approach tougher encounters discreetly, and possibly gain the upper hand with a powerful backstab. A successful backstab takes away a lot of posture and health, and in some cases, when the posture is fully drained, it outright kills the enemy on a single hit.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/31a616070ad06c7985fa8bb08b52eca685c72de2.gif[/img]

[h3]Spectre Blaster[/h3]
The Spectre Blaster is attuned for staggering foes, rather than dealing damage. It is a supporting tool for melee combat with which one can interrupt dangerous attacks. The Spectre Blaster holds a single slug and can be reloaded by slaying an enemy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/69ef6f00c38575dfc64ff0fa1545740eb1f2b621.gif[/img]

[h3]Dash[/h3]
Dash allows you to make a quick evasive move in any direction. This move is good for dodging smaller attacks and gaining an advantage during combat as it uses less of the Striver’s stamina.

[h3]Dodge Roll[/h3]
Perform a Dodge Roll to avoid larger attacks. The player is invulnerable while dodge rolling, and although you can dodge a greater distance, it will cost you more stamina.

[h3]Lunge Attack [/h3]
This move is earned separately through a Blessing. You can Lunge Attack from a dodge roll, which allows for the evasive manoeuvre to be used as an offensive move.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/fc10c018df5c11cd7f3ec42bac8db710827e360d.png[/img]

We have come a long way since our previous release, Morbid: The Seven Acolytes, and want to thank everyone who has played the demo and given us feedback, which we are constantly reading through. 

Whilst we appreciate all the souls-like fans, it’s important to note that we’re not trying to represent a souls-like game but a more fast-paced hack-and-slash action game with souls-like elements. Morbid: The Lords of Ire is continuously under development and we will keep making the combat in our game the best it can be!

And lastly, we thought we’d show you some behind-the-scenes shots of the motion captures taken by the developers at the Still Running studio. Almost every animation you see in-game is created in real life using motion capture (and yes, that is the CEO of Still Running stumbling around)...enjoy!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/8275d9b9d3569e2cdd54da216b5f7cdb2c32b351.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/85432a954fd42bb1a889b50f79dadf72286f1ced.gif[/img]
[i]One of the first motion captures we ever did for Morbid: The Lords of Ire (Cosmian Reborn enemy)[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/a9386ee4c9a7b2e6ec79f3d092f0507b7a87f00a.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/b18fa56ba40904dcf253f8027aaca7045766c85d.gif[/img]
[i]Another early motion capture session for the Tusker Champion enemy[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/7c5467f0a883f0c817391c6c320617363fc37923.png[/img]
[i]Having fun with Battle Brute (props are important!)[/i]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/fc10c018df5c11cd7f3ec42bac8db710827e360d.png[/img]

notes.title: Developer Diary #5 - Weapons
notes.content:
Greetings, Striver!

This month, we would like to show you just some of the gut-wrenching and powerful weapons that you will find in Morbid: The Lords of Ire. Which will you choose to slaughter the hideous creatures that await your path? 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/fc10c018df5c11cd7f3ec42bac8db710827e360d.png[/img]


[h3][b]Sword of Dibrom[/b][/h3]

The Sword of Dibrom is a legendary sword that the Striver is allotted at the beginning of her gruesome journey. Every Striver receives the sword when they first begin their training. It is a fine sword and has served the Striver well through many dire scenarios. Though its power has waned over the years, the blade still reminds her of the path she has hitherto fared.

[i]“The sword still reminds you of the path you've hitherto fared. Its warm hilt has guided you through the cursed hamlet of Solya, the murky streets of Yortael, the putrid Felfields, and the deadly maze that was Grimwald's Grove.

By its trusty blade, many a mighty foe has fallen, the mindless Boatswain Borga, the legless witch Yaga Moer, the formidable Undead Mammoth-Beast, and of course, the Seven Acolytes of Mornia.”[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/0fb045e5add6b66042a62ffe0d0976752e578afd.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/c86c9b07944cabbcb4a962808e320304955713aa.png[/img]
[i]The Sword of Dibrom is a legendary sword that the Striver is allotted at the beginning of her gruesome journey. [/i]


[h3][b]Mountain’s Edge[/b][/h3]

Great axes trade away speed for high damage and impact. Most designs thus endorse a barbaric style of combat where ferocity reigns and grace matters not. Those who favor the brutish way of the great axe often declare that in battle elegance is irrelevant; only the results matter. One could say they are not wrong.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/829bcd85eeee1b4dd0f388fcd696b81abc2b30a1.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/b7bd6786a969a7b0a95496a49a8127abb14fb155.png[/img]
[i]Mountain’s Edge is a Two-Handed executioner's Great Axe of Rimeholdian origin, named after the mountain itself.[/i]


[h3][b]Fists of Ire[/b][/h3]

Knuckle dusters have historically been a popular weapon class among the martial artists of Ire. Various designs and materials have been used in making these so-called, iron fists. Though low in damage across the board, they all share one distinguishing feature; they provide the combattant with superior control over their maneuvers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/f78f7b4079cc65ee68042f68e987e549d75fb7a0.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/4babe2061299e4a72180a7a810aaededaa20593c.png[/img]
[i]Fists of Ire are Iron fists forged in Irelia and are part of the capital's own high-quality weapon family. [/i]


[h3][b]Flensing Daggers[/b][/h3]

Daggers allow for a combat rhythm of unparalleled rapidity. No other weapon class can match the speed with which a combatant armed with two deadly dirks can take on an enemy. However, the swift moves are being paid for in diminished damage and impact, as small blades create small wounds and carry little inertia.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/4f2f3445c06a410f4e4bbf259255c43dafb25207.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/07b76bb398f2704bfb6cfb91d373f97f799d1b21.png[/img]

[i]Flensing Daggers are from Dunghaven, historically used by the fishermen of yore for flensing their catch.[/i]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/fc10c018df5c11cd7f3ec42bac8db710827e360d.png[/img]

notes.title: Developer Diary #4 - Blessings
notes.content:
Yuletide Blessings to you, Striver!

We hope that you have all had a festive and merry Yuletide season! As an extra little gift, we're here to bring you a sneak peak into the Blessings feature in [b]Morbid: The Lords of Ire[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/fc10c018df5c11cd7f3ec42bac8db710827e360d.png[/img]

Similarly to Morbid: The Seven Acolytes, the Blessings in [b]Morbid: The Lords of Ire[/b] allows the player to build their character by levelling up and customising the skillset of the Striver in even more varied and tangible ways.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/ebbd583ce858c228b101db0bd935c0859a5fb327.png[/img]

The Blessings can be found one by one as you progress through the game and find artifacts (Tomes of Insight) which you return to Yan, the Blessed One, in the Hall of Redemption to be deciphered.
Yan also allows you to upgrade tiers and buy more slots for your Blessings using Skill Points. There are maximum of three Blessing Slots, each upgradeable up to level three.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/fc10c018df5c11cd7f3ec42bac8db710827e360d.png[/img]

[h3][b]Blessing of the Healer[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/3b87d817eaea66b3742daf7e0d4788a6a0e5a132.png[/img]
[i]*Blessing Card Concept Art[/i]

Blessing of the Healer gifts the player with a larger Health Bar.
With higher Tiers, it will improve healing effects and give the player another life.

[h3][b]Blessing of the Acrobat[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/19e75ee0e9c31d795063a75777dca3c0446e4f1b.png[/img]
[i]*Blessing Card Concept Art[/i]

Blessing of the Acrobat gifts the player a larger Stamina Bar.
With higher Tiers it regenerates Stamina faster and removes Stamina downtime.

[h3][b]Blessing of the Gunslinger[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/ae4e1199dfc302eb7b45550f46aec54bb55ec19b.png[/img]
[i]*Blessing Card Concept Art[/i]

Blessing of the Gunslinger gifts the player with shots that have more impact.
With higher Tiers the player obtains Piercing Bullets and doubles the Ammo cap.

These 3 Blessings are just some of what you will get to experience in [b]Morbid: The Lords of Ire[/b], and there will be many more unique and useful Blessings to come in the full game!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/fc10c018df5c11cd7f3ec42bac8db710827e360d.png[/img]

Don't forget to prepare for your battle against evil by [b]adding Morbid: The Lords of Ire to your Steam Wishlist today[/b].

notes.title: Developer Diary #3 - Environments
notes.content:
Greetings, Striver!

The land of Ire has been divided into five realms, governed by the five factions and led by the five Acolyte leaders - [b]'The Lords of Ire'[/b].

In Morbid: The Lords of Ire, you must battle your way through these realms, facing horrid monstrosities, special encounters and quests. Ultimately, one by one, it is your goal to defeat the five Acolyte lords.

Get a taste of the stricken land of Ire by checking out just some of the environments you will battle across, in hopes of freeing from the evil grip of the Gahars, below...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/fc10c018df5c11cd7f3ec42bac8db710827e360d.png[/img]

[h2]RIMEHOLD[/h2]

[i]"For ages, the stoic warriors of Rimehold were the noble watchmen of the Wintry Mountains. With pride and vigilance, they guarded the mountain passage between Mornia and Ire."[/i]

Often referred to as 'The Wintry Mountains', this snowbound realm is one of the first gruesome lands that you will visit in this action-adventure.

Tread through deep snowy passes and explore frozen stone strongholds in Rimehold, home to the forever-doomed living and dead accursed warriors.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/8a6ae3a66e3822a26c680915fd112f78abebf5da.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/689712b84b4d5281c10e2c47cd2598fa755c7ff6.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/53f8ef5c2a008fb118bd6bbcd3f1470a8170a90d.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/fc10c018df5c11cd7f3ec42bac8db710827e360d.png[/img]

[h2]IRELIA[/h2]

[i]"As the onslaught continued, most Irelians fled the city, but some refused to flee. Those who stayed split into two factions: Some tried to defend the city against the insect invaders, while others chose not to fight but to worship the monstrosities as their new overlords."[/i]

The monumental capital of Ire, Irelia fell into ruin when a colony of parasitic insect demons invaded the city.

Ruled by the Cult of Culex, an evil communion, Irelia features towering citadels and gothic-Victorian architecture. Away from the blood-drenched streets, players can also explore the [i]Rejectorium[/i] - the orphanage of Irelia.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/e6eda5ee411f7c01d31d58d13444e44a81694225.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/b1013ead66887fb8538f12f516f8bd5af8e84b82.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/b8eafe6893f892a787a32feed292337c083b9684.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/fc10c018df5c11cd7f3ec42bac8db710827e360d.png[/img]

[h2]HALL OF REDEMPTION[/h2]

[i]"You made it back, Striver! What news from Rimehold? …So—it is as I feared. The great corruptors are among us once more. The Gahars have returned."[/i]

Formerly known as the Cathedral of Wrath, the Hall of Redemption is the commemorative hall where the last Striver defeated Inquisitor Odius and Redeemed Mornia in [b]Morbid: The Seven Acolytes[/b].

Players will be able to use the Hall of Redemption as a hub to upgrade their abilities and equipment, or seek shelter from the morbid world outside.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/d52141d2af44a91c244c1e45096a08789403dbca.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/b882a0b1bc65d6dbb459078fa7c474ea04bc2dc9.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/e774bfd3a57ca84b517bcd339fc61bce6142c156.png[/img]
[i]All in-game images are still work-in-progress, and may change before release![/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/fc10c018df5c11cd7f3ec42bac8db710827e360d.png[/img]

Be wary, Striver, for there are more gruesome Realms that await you in Morbid: The Lords of Ire...

notes.title: Developer Diary #1 - The Striver
notes.content:
[h3][i]"By redeeming Mornia, and liberating the kingdom from under the sway of the Gahars and their Acolytes, the last Striver of Dibrom so completed her sacred mission. But while her mission ended, her duty resumed, for even with all the Acolytes slain, the Gahars themselves never truly died."[/i][/h3]

As you may have seen from our new store capsule imagery, [b]The Striver[/b] has become a much bigger focus of Morbid: The Lords of Ire, as the Morbid franchise shifts from 2D pixel-art to 3D immersion

The brand-new featured art from the team at Still Running gives us our first detailed look at our fearless protagonist, Striver.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/79932700cd360b67b66ab1560650148101c7de2d.png[/img]

Players of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1140890/Morbid_The_Seven_Acolytes/][b]Morbid: The Seven Acolytes[/b][/url] will recognise our main protagonist of the game's sequel, Morbid: The Lords of Ire. Years after defeating the [b]Seven Acolytes[/b] and liberating the kingdom of [b]Mornia[/b] from evil, [b]Striver[/b] returns as duty calls upon her once more, as another set of abysmal Acolytes await to be slain.

In [b]Morbid: The Lords of Ire[/b], players will be able to [b]"Become The Striver"[/b], taking control of the gutsy heroine and experiencing a visceral 3D world in third-person view. We can't wait for players to step into the shoes of The Last Striver of Dibrom and explore the gore-fueled worlds that await you.
